request: All commands are flat JSON objects with op and required fields. Implement read {id} returning exactly {id,body,version}, and write {id,expected_version,body} returning {ok:true,version:new_version}. IDs are positive integers; expected_version is a required nonnegative integer; body is a required nonempty string. Read or write of a missing document returns {error:"not_found"}. A mismatching expected_version returns {error:"stale"}. Invalid input returns {error:"invalid"}. Write increments the existing version by one and appends the new body/version to history. Document update and history insertion are one transaction with row locking; any failure rolls back both. History is unique by (document_id,version). Unexpected database failures return {error:"db_error"}, not RPC errors. Parameterize SQL, use the injected official client, and preserve data across service restarts.
transaction_requirements: Lock the document and compare expected_version; increment/update and append history atomically.
Rollback both document and history on failure; history unique by (document_id,version).

request: Use flat JSON commands with op and all listed fields required. location {user_id} returns exactly {user_id,slot_id}. move {user_id,to_slot} returns {ok:true}. Both fields are positive integers; invalid input returns {error:"invalid"}. Missing users or target slots return {error:"not_found"}. A target slot with enabled=0 returns {error:"disabled"}. A target occupied by another user returns {error:"occupied"}. Moving to the same current slot returns success without changes. Check and update in a row-locking transaction; each user has one placement and a slot may contain only one user. Unexpected database failures return {error:"db_error"} and must roll back. Never expose raw database errors; use parameterized SQL and the injected official client. Data survives service restarts.
transaction_requirements: Row-lock source placement and target slot/occupancy before relocation.
Preserve unique user and unique slot ownership; rollback any failed relocation.

request: All commands are flat JSON with op and required fields. read {team_id} returns exactly {team_id,revision,members:[{member_id,role}]} with members ordered by member_id ascending. replace {team_id,expected_revision,members} returns {ok:true,revision:new_revision}. team_id and member_id are positive integers; expected_revision is required and nonnegative; members is a nonempty array of entries with required nonempty role strings. Invalid input returns {error:"invalid"}. Missing teams return {error:"not_found"}; revision mismatch returns {error:"stale"}; duplicate member IDs within one replacement return {error:"conflict"}. Lock the team and replace its complete member set in one transaction: increment revision, delete old members, insert all new members. Failure in any insert must restore both old members and old revision. Members are unique by (team_id,member_id), and reference their team. Unexpected database failures return {error:"db_error"} with nil Go error. Parameterize SQL, use the injected official client, preserve data across restarts, and do not maintain records in process memory.
transaction_requirements: Lock and compare team revision; update revision, delete previous members and insert replacement set atomically.
Rollback parent revision and deleted/inserted members on any failure; unique by (team_id,member_id).
